title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure. An AI-generated video presented a real public figure as endorsing an investment, and the fabricated endorsement did the work of a credential. The synthetic video sat at the front of the fraud, at the point where trust is established and before any money moves. Everything after it, the WhatsApp contact, the multiple accounts, the remote access to the victim's computer, depended on that first acceptance.

The check that was missing is verification of the endorsement itself. A named celebrity appearing in a video is not evidence that the person made the claim, and the Police Service of Northern Ireland said as much when it noted that apparent celebrity endorsements do not prove an investment is genuine. Confirming that a firm is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority, and confirming who one is actually dealing with, are the steps police pointed to. The victim had no practical way to test the video, and the fraudsters supplied the only channel through which the investment could be questioned.

What is not established is who produced the video, which public figure was depicted, and whether anyone has been charged. Police did not name the celebrity, and the loss figure is what the PSNI reported rather than an adjudicated sum. BBC News NI has seen similar scams using the names of other financial and business figures, which shows a pattern of reuse and not that any of those people endorsed anything.

reports.title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

summary:
A person in the Ards and north Down area lost £250,000 in an investment scam, the Police Service of Northern Ireland said. The victim saw an AI generated video that appeared to feature a well known financial sector personality. It promoted an investment opportunity and claimed significant returns. After a small initial investment, the victim was contacted on WhatsApp and encouraged to pay more. The fraudsters persuaded them to open multiple online accounts and gave remote access to their computer, saying they were helping with the investment. Police called it a sophisticated fraud.

The scammers gained the victim's trust and urged them to borrow money to keep investing, with funds sent to criminal controlled accounts. Police did not name the celebrity. BBC News NI has seen similar scams using financial experts Martin Lewis, Peter Jones and Steven Bartlett. The PSNI said apparent celebrity endorsements do not prove an investment is genuine. Superintendent Joanne Gibson urged people to stop and check financial activity and families to discuss fraud. Police advised verifying who people deal with and checking Financial Conduct Authority authorisation.
title_en: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity
